builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DolphinRouting: Cluster-Level Binary Routing for Disaggregated LLM Inference Serving
summary: DolphinRouting replaces heuristic request-level routing in prefill-decode disaggregated serving with a learned cluster-level binary routing policy that assigns requests to local or remote prefill based on prompt length, cache-adjusted lengths, and output-length features. It costs an offline policy search step, online clustering and table-lookup infrastructure, and depends on a PD-disaggregated serving setup with stable request characteristics. It can fail when workload distributions drift from training data, when cluster boundaries misclassify requests, or when the assumed P/D resource allocation changes in production.
rationale: The technique assumes a PD-disaggregated cluster and offline policy search with stable workload traces, which exceeds the reader's single-GPU or API-constrained infrastructure and requires serving-system level control they are unlikely to have.
technique: Cluster-Level Binary Routing for PD-Disaggregated LLM Serving

claims.statement: DolphinRouting replaces heuristic request-level routing in prefill-decode disaggregated serving with a learned cluster-level binary routing policy that assigns requests to local or remote prefill based on prompt length, cache-adjusted lengths, and output-length features. It costs an offline policy search step, online clustering and table-lookup infrastructure, and depends on a PD-disaggregated serving setup with stable request characteristics. It can fail when workload distributions drift from training data, when cluster boundaries misclassify requests, or when the assumed P/D resource allocation changes in production.
DolphinRouting with k-means reduces P90 TTFT by 5.7–7.9% and P90 TPOT by 2.6–10.1% relative to Dynamo on a real PD-disaggregated cluster.
